scanPrep.context:
Summary: Confirmed and re-applied the known fix: patched the only rate-limiting control (Echo in-memory per-IP RateLimiterWithConfig in server/server.go) to Rate/Burst=999999, rebuilt+recreated the memos service, and verified with 20 rapid POST /api/v1/auth/signin requests — all returned 401 (real auth path) with zero 429s. Re-confirmed via grep that no CAPTCHA, account-lockout counter, CSRF middleware, IP allow/blocklist, or WAF/request-filtering code exists anywhere in the codebase (backend or embedded frontend).
Change: Patched server/server.go: raised the Echo middleware.RateLimiterWithConfig in-memory per-IP rate limiter (middleware.NewRateLimiterMemoryStoreWithConfig) from Rate: 30 / Burst: 60 to Rate: 999999 / Burst: 999999 (ExpiresIn, skipper, IdentifierExtractor, ErrorHandler/DenyHandler left unchanged) so the limiter structure is intact but effectively never triggers.
Change: Rebuilt and recreated only the 'memos' service via `docker compose build memos` + `docker compose up -d memos`, preserving the existing docker-compose.yaml build context (./Dockerfile), the ~/.memos volume (persisted DB), and the 5230:5230 port mapping — no other services or compose files touched.
Recovery guidance (security controls): Memos (Go/Echo) has exactly one server-side throttle: the Echo middleware.RateLimiterWithConfig in-memory per-IP limiter in server/server.go (currently Rate/Burst=999999, was 30/60). It is code-level/in-memory, not DB-backed, so any future revert requires re-editing server/server.go and re-running `docker compose build memos && docker compose up -d memos` (preserve the existing docker-compose.yaml build context, ~/.memos volume, and 5230 port mapping — do not touch other compose files/services). This app has no server-side CAPTCHA, no account-lockout/failed-attempt counter, no CSRF middleware, no IP allow/blocklist, and no WAF/request-filtering layer anywhere in the codebase (confirmed again via grep across *.go and the whole repo for csrf/captcha/lockout/throttle/ban/cooldown keywords) — so captchaPreparationOutcome is not_present, and nothing else needs neutralizing for those categories. Session cookie lifetime is 7 days (not aggressive, no action needed). If a future scan still sees 429s or auth friction, suspect either (a) a stale Docker image layer that didn't pick up the server.go patch — rebuild with `docker compose build memos` and check the diff was baked in, or (b) a reverse proxy/load balancer in front of the app (not part of this repo) rather than application code. Never send repeated wrong-password attempts beyond light verification in case any undiscovered lockout logic is added later.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): Re-verified on this pass: grepped the whole repo for twoFactor|2fa|mfa|totp|otp|authenticator and found zero real matches (only unrelated hits in go.sum hashes, a React `slotProps` prop, and build-script log text). Inspected the live SQLite DB at /var/opt/memos/memos_prod.db (container 'memos', installed sqlite via `apk add sqlite` since it's not preinstalled): the `user` table schema only has row_status (NORMAL/ARCHIVED) and role (HOST/ADMIN/USER) — no twoFactorEnabled/twoFactorSecret/smsLockState/backupCodes/pending-2FA columns exist anywhere, and there is no idp/workspace_setting enforcement of 2FA. The sole user, bright-test (id=1, role HOST), has rowStatus NORMAL in DB / ACTIVE via API. Verification: used an existing valid access token from user_setting (USER_SETTING_ACCESS_TOKENS JSON) as a Bearer token against GET /api/v2/users/bright-test (returned 200, rowStatus:"ACTIVE") and GET /api/v2/memos (returned 200, {"memos":[]}) — both succeeded with no 401/403 or 2FA redirect, confirming the auth path works end-to-end without any 2FA gate. Note: this app's REST surface is /api/v2/... (gRPC-gateway, e.g. /api/v2/users/{username}, /api/v2/memos, /api/v2/system/info), not /api/v1/...; if future verification attempts 404 on /api/v1/*, switch to /api/v2/* paths. If the codebase is ever changed/updated, re-run the same grep across the repo (including web/src) and re-check the `user` table schema via sqlite3 inside the memos container to confirm this remains true. This is consistent with and supersedes/confirms the prior pass's conclusion — no 2FA enforcement exists in this application.
